briefHtml:
NAV S$10,314,194 — oil re-spikes on the Iran rejection cycle (WTI +2.8% $92.87, Brent +5.8% ~$102); 10y eases off 5.342% (highest since 2002) to 5.25% into tonight's NFP (watcher −0.507%; ≈flat −0.02% vs restated base) · listed flag −2.749% (no rule trip) · 4 critical flags: 3 false (day 4), 1 REAL — CDL · Oct 1 restated UP +S$1.4k

  • Biggest mover: oil — and in the book, CDL. Trump rejected Iran's latest offer (“simply not enough”; the reported offer was IAEA access for sanctions relief, denied by IRNA), told Time that bombing could ramp up after the midterms and that Iran must sign “or it will no longer exist”; WSJ: a third carrier strike group plus up to 10,000 troops by end-November, and Trump expects to resume bombing in November. WTI +2.8% to $92.87, Brent +5.8% to ~$102.31; a supertanker burned off Oman. In the book: CDL −3.5% to ~S$7.12 on 3.5x volume — a fourth straight down day since GET+ (8.26 → ~7.12 = −13.8%).
  • The one thing: the flag glitch finally caught a real one. Three of four flags are wrong a fourth day (verified Thursday: GDX −1.21%, SILJ −0.62%, SLVP −0.34% vs flags of −6.1%/−6.3%/−5.6%), but the CDL flag (−13.4%) is the post-GET+ cumulative break measured off a stale baseline — real, and near the 52-week low (6.87). Verify before acting, and before dismissing. Macro: the long end blinked — the 10y printed 5.342% intraday (highest since April 2002) then eased to 5.25% as Jefferson (“may need more time”) and Bowman (“no urgent need”) pushed back; NFP tonight 8:30pm SGT (cons ~90–100k) is the gate, with ISM prices at 77.9 and Brent at $102 arguing the other way.

Risk flags — 4 critical: three false (day 4), one real

  • Flags: GDX −6.1% · SILJ −6.3% · SLVP −5.6% · CDL −13.4%. Verified Thursday: GDX $86.74 −1.21% · SILJ $27.11 −0.62% · SLVP $34.85 −0.34% (first capture in ~6 sessions) · CDL ~S$7.12 −3.5% on the day, −13.8% over four sessions from S$8.26 — REAL (GET+ strategic review voted down: S$5B invest / S$6B divest FY27–29, gearing 75%→55%, S$7.8B fund-management target, up-to-S$1.12 special dividend; brokers still 'buy' at ~31% NAV discount).
  • Listed-book flag −2.749% — below the −3% rule, no trip; flag math still unverified.

Position moves (verified Thursday)

  • US ETFs: GDX $86.74 −1.21% · GDXJ −1.31% · SILJ $27.11 −0.62% · SLVP $34.85 −0.34% · SIL −0.44% · NEM −0.58% · SLV $55.02 +0.94% · GLD $382.76 +0.50%. Spot gold +0.4% ~$4,183; spot silver ~$60.7 holding above $60; USAGOLD: physical silver demand doubling.
  • HK closed Thursday (National Day), reopens today; mainland shut until Oct 8. Last closes Wed: Tencent 431.00 (tell 439 broken, line 425) · SMIC 60.65 · Xiaomi 25.24.
  • SGX Thursday: STI 5,667.67 −0.14% · CDL ~7.12 −3.5% (3.5x volume) · UOL 8.20 +0.49% · Keppel 11.16 −1.06% · Sembcorp +1.73% · SGX −0.18% · STE +0.64%. Singapore home prices accelerating (Bloomberg) — CDL is company-specific.
  • US Thursday: S and P 7,666 +0.19% · NDX +0.31% · Dow 50,932 +0.04% · VIX 16.39 · 10y 5.25% (intraday 5.342%, highest since Apr 2002) · DXY 102.00 +0.5%. Software led (Accenture beat, Synopsys raised guidance on OpenAI deal); Micron +3%; Alphabet +2% (new Gemini); Anthropic eyeing IPO as soon as mid-Nov (Bloomberg).

Insider / Congress

  • Wing Tai (W05.SI): director-interest run holds at 18 September filings (latest Sep 29; none Sep 30–Oct 1); Sep 30 brought Special + Final Dividend notices, Annual Report 2026 and the 62nd AGM notice. No dealings found for other held SGX names or HK names (Tencent/SMIC/Xiaomi).
  • Congress: no new STOCK Act filings since the Sep 28 batch — CT Senate Democrat private-LLC churn (MH Built to Last / Days Between / Not Fade Away, mixed buys and sells), OK-1 House Republican wholesale equity sell-down into Oklahoma muni bonds (dozens of names incl. LMT, XOM, HD), OH-7 House Republican Mercato Partners LP buy $1K–$15K. Nothing in held tickers.

Trump / policy watch

  • Iran rejected, escalation dated: offer rejected as “simply not enough”; “sign a deal or it will no longer exist”; WSJ — third carrier group + up to 10k troops by end-Nov, bombing expected to resume in November; supertanker burning off Oman. WTI +2.8% $92.87, Brent +5.8% ~$102.31.
  • Long end blinked: 10y 5.342% intraday (highest since Apr 2002) → 5.25%; Jefferson “may need more time”, Bowman “no urgent need”; Kashkari open-minded on October; Trump: rising rates “pretty bad”, “wants Warsh to vote the way he wants”.
  • ISM prices surge: headline 54.5 missed, but Prices Paid 77.9 (exp 72.3); claims 197k; NFP tonight cons ~90–100k.
  • Energy security: US warned France/Germany to release emergency diesel stocks or face possible export ban; EU taskforce meets today; SPR to be filled with Venezuelan oil; Gulf exports −26% y/y during the conflict, prices +44% YTD.
  • China trade: US moving to use China's dependence on US aviation suppliers as leverage; Greer — unconditional MFN tariffs “warrant reform”.
  • AI tape: software-led (Accenture, Synopsys/OpenAI guidance raise); Micron +3%; Alphabet +2% (Gemini); Anthropic IPO chatter for mid-Nov.

Risk

  • Flag glitch day 4: 3 false, 1 real (CDL) — stale-baseline pattern; verify all flags. L46.SI price error 16th session.
  • Silver line: 1,777 oz × ~$60.71 × 1.2803 ≈ S$138.1k vs ~S$56.24k loan → equity ≈ S$81.9k ≈ 1.69x; a −5.9% silver day ≈ −10% equity.
  • Long end paused not peaked: 30y ~5.66%; NFP tonight is the gate; Brent $102 re-opens the October hike on a hot print.
  • Iran escalation calendar: carriers + troops by end-Nov, bombing expected to resume in November.
  • HK reopens today on holiday-thin tape; mainland shut until Oct 8; Tencent 431 with tell 439 broken.
  • FX: ~35% NW non-SGD; USDSGD 1.2803 (softer SGD); DXY 102.00; USDCNY ≈ 6.70.
  • ~62% of the liquid book idle cash; Oct 1 restated UP +S$1.4k (first up-night; cumulative ≈ −S$86k).

Alpha — signals, not advice

  • Defense sleeve (15% vs ~0%): first long-end pause (5.342% → 5.25% on Jefferson/Bowman). NFP tonight is the second gate: a print at/below ~70k with the 10y holding under ~5.25% = first-tranche entry; hot print or 10y back over 5.34% = wait; Brent $102 is the wild card.
  • HK AI barbell (Asia 10% vs ~3%; AI 15% vs ~1%): HK reopens today; US AI tape improved (Micron +3%, Gemini, Synopsys/OpenAI, Anthropic IPO). Watch reopen direction; no volume confirmation until Oct 8; 439 reclaim with southbound the trigger, 425 the line.
  • Silver/miners (real assets 20%): flags wrong day 4; SLV +0.94%, spot ~$60.7 holding above $60; physical demand doubling; ISM prices 77.9 + Brent $102 = inflation tailwind vs DXY 102 headwind. Suspension below $62 stands; $62 reclaim with a stalling dollar re-arms the sleeve.

trumpWatch.title: Iran offer rejected ("simply not enough"); WSJ: third carrier group + up to 10k troops by end-November, bombing expected to resume in November — oil re-spikes
trumpWatch.detail: Trump rejected Iran's latest offer — reported by Bloomberg as restored IAEA inspector access to bombed facilities in exchange for sanctions relief (IRNA denies) — calling it "simply not enough" (US press, Oct 2 SGT). To Time Magazine: bombing could ramp up after the midterms; Iran must sign "or it will no longer exist." WSJ: third carrier strike group + additional Marine ships + up to 10,000 troops, arrival by end-November; Trump told aides he expects to resume bombing in November; Roosevelt crew preparing extended deployment. A 2.5M-bbl supertanker was reported hit and burning 8km off Oman (Fars). Pezeshkian: Tehran "will never shy away from dialogue." Oil: WTI +2.8% to $92.87, Brent +5.8% to ~$102.31.

trumpWatch.title: Long end blinks: 10y prints 5.342% intraday (highest since April 2002), then eases to 5.25% on Jefferson/Bowman; Trump leans on Warsh
trumpWatch.detail: Treasuries bull-steepened: Jefferson (voter) said the Fed "may need more time before deciding its next rate move" and that bond yields show markets reassessing the outlook; Bowman (voter) sees "no urgent need" for more moves this year; Kashkari is open-minded on an October hike (one more pencilled this year, another in 2027); Cook: "AI is causing pockets of inflation"; Schmid: rising long-term rates "beginning to affect more parts of the economy." Treasury liquidity buyback accepted $6.0B of $46.4B offered. Trump: rising rates are "pretty bad," high rates hurt more than inflation, "certain levels of inflation help pay off debt," and he "wants Warsh to vote the way he wants."

trumpWatch.title: ISM September: headline misses at 54.5 (exp 55.0) but Prices Paid surges to 77.9 (exp 72.3) — NFP tonight, cons ~90-100k
trumpWatch.detail: ISM manufacturing 54.5 vs 55.0 expected (prev 54.6); Prices Paid 77.9 vs 72.3 expected (prev 71.1) — a supply-shock signature with oil re-spiking; new orders 55.3 and employment 52.7 both improved; S and P Global final 55.9 (exp 57.0). Jobless claims 197K; continuing claims 1,701K; Challenger layoffs 43.3K (from 52.9K); Revelio September payrolls +56.9k. NFP Friday 8:30pm SGT: consensus ~90-100k vs 162k prior (ADP printed 90k Wednesday).

trumpWatch.title: Energy security: US warns France/Germany to release emergency diesel stocks or face possible export ban; SPR to be filled with Venezuelan oil
trumpWatch.detail: The US told France and Germany to release emergency diesel stocks or face a possible export ban; Energy Secretary Wright is "highly confident" Europe will help and said gasoline/diesel prices "will be lower by the election"; Bessent pressed European partners to accelerate deliveries; the EU Energy Union Taskforce meets Friday on coordinated releases. Trump: the US will fill the SPR with Venezuelan oil "at very little cost" (Venezuela September exports 1.08M bpd, 629k to the US). Gulf producers exported 26% fewer barrels during the conflict while prices rose 44% YTD (Tanker Trackers); Saudi East-West pipeline back to ~5.5M bpd (Argus).

trumpWatch.title: China trade: US moves to use Beijing's dependence on US aviation suppliers as leverage; Greer: unconditional MFN tariffs "warrant reform"
trumpWatch.detail: The administration is taking steps to use China's dependence on US aviation suppliers as leverage in trade negotiations — a pressure point aimed at the aviation supply chain, relevant to the China/HK tech theme. USTR Greer: the US is on track for record goods trade exports this year, the concept of unconditional most-favoured-nation tariffs "warrants reform," and the US is open to a Canada deal "although gaps remain."

trumpWatch.title: AI tape: software leads (Accenture beat, Synopsys raises guidance on OpenAI deal); Micron +3%; Alphabet +2% on new Gemini; Anthropic eyeing IPO as soon as mid-November
trumpWatch.detail: NDX +0.31% led Thursday: Accenture's strong earnings lifted software, Synopsys gained after raising guidance following its deal with OpenAI, Micron rose ~3% in follow-through to Wednesday's blowout, Alphabet +2% on the newest Gemini model, NVDA +1.1%. Bloomberg: Anthropic is eyeing an IPO as soon as mid-November. Read-through to the AI-bottleneck theme, the memory complex (Samsung/SK Hynix) and HK tech reopening Friday.
